details:
GANDIVA MECHSAT – Autonomous Orbital Repair, Refuelling and Satellite Servicing System

GANDIVA MECHSAT is a proposed autonomous orbital servicing spacecraft designed to support the repair, maintenance and refuelling of compatible satellites. The project explores a future where satellites can potentially receive servicing and continue their missions instead of being replaced immediately when certain technical failures or fuel limitations occur.

Satellites are essential for communication, navigation, weather forecasting, Earth observation and scientific research. However, fuel depletion and technical failures can reduce their operational lifetimes. Replacing satellites can require additional manufacturing, financial resources and launches. MECHSAT proposes an alternative approach through a dedicated mobile orbital servicing vehicle supported by a permanent facility called MECHSAT STATION.

System Architecture

MECHSAT has three major structural sections.

1. Front Section – Intelligent Manipulator Circle

The front section contains a circular robotic hub divided into eight geometrical segments, supporting eight specialised robotic arms. Two arms are dedicated to multispectral AI cameras for observation, one arm is assigned to fuel-line routing, and five arms are designed for mechanical intervention.

The design incorporates a central titanium hub ring, electrical slip rings and retractable tool bays with PTFE-lined channels and proposed piezoelectric actuators.

2. Middle Section – Solar Octagon Core

The middle section is an eight-sided prism surrounded by solar-tracking panels. It supports the spacecraft's central computing systems and proposed energy-generation architecture using gallium arsenide solar cells.

3. Back Section – Co-axial Propellant Modality and Lander

The back section contains an inner pressurised sphere assigned to xenon ion-propulsion fuel and an outer coaxial cylinder assigned to satellite-refuelling propellant. It also incorporates vertical landing pads.

VYOMO GUIDE AI

MECHSAT includes a proposed autonomous intelligence architecture called VYOMO GUIDE AI. It consists of four major algorithms:

- Collision-Avoidance Pathing to coordinate robotic-arm movements.
- Dynamic Mass Tracking to estimate changing spacecraft centre of gravity.
- Counter-Thrust Pulse Programme to address forces generated during propellant transfer.
- Active Thermal Modulation to manage proposed cooling systems and insulation.

Engineering and Scientific Principles

The project incorporates carbon-fibre structural materials, graphene heat pipes, mu-metal shielding and gallium arsenide solar cells. Its scientific foundation includes orbital velocity, Newton's Third Law, Hohmann transfers and atmospheric thermal protection.

MECHSAT also identifies engineering challenges involving mechanical stress, thermal expansion, fluid-transfer forces and rotating electrical connections, with specific proposed mitigation systems.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The primary intended impact is to explore satellite life extension through compatible refuelling and modular repairs. This could potentially reduce premature satellite replacement, improve the use of existing orbital infrastructure and contribute to more sustainable space operations.

The project also explores autonomous robotics, AI-based spacecraft coordination and future orbital servicing infrastructure.

MECHSAT has defined operational limitations: it targets only compatible satellites with suitable refuelling interfaces and selected modular repair architectures. Its proposed role involving non-cooperative structural debris is limited to mechanical stabilisation.

Creativity and Development Tools

The creativity of MECHSAT lies in integrating an eight-arm robotic architecture, a solar octagon core, separate propulsion and servicing propellant arrangements, and an autonomous AI control concept into one proposed orbital servicing platform.

ChatGPT and Google Gemini were used as AI-assisted development tools for project explanations and content development. ChatGPT also assisted with website content and coding. Canva was used to design and publish the project website and create presentation slides. The engineering concept and project architecture were developed by Team GANDIVA.

The project considers mechanical stability, spacecraft mass, thermal management, electrical interference, orbital movement, compatibility and operational safety.

GANDIVA MECHSAT is currently an engineering concept, not a demonstrated operational spacecraft. Further simulation, calculations, prototype development and validation are required.

GANDIVA MECHSAT – Engineering a More Sustainable Future in Space.
